title: GCD Or HCF
problemStatement: Compute GCD/HCF of two integers. Often used to compute LCM = a / gcd * b carefully.
intuition: Euclid: gcd(a,b)=gcd(b, a%b). Remainders shrink quickly → O(log min(a,b)). This is the interview algorithm — not trial from min down to 1.

approaches.title: Brute: trial from min(a,b)
approaches.idea: Check downward for first common divisor.

approaches.title: Optimal: Euclidean algorithm
approaches.whyWorks: Any common divisor of a and b also divides a%b; the sets of common divisors stay aligned.

specialTechnique.title: Special technique: Euclidean algorithm
specialTechnique.body: Remainders strictly decrease for b>0, so termination is guaranteed. This underpins fraction simplification, modular inverses (extended Euclid), and LCM calculations.

commonMistakes: Brute trial for huge values → TLE
patternRecognition: Fraction reduction, lattice points, frog jumps with steps
interviewInsight: Brute vs Euclid is a clean complexity conversation — take it.
